\subsection{E2: decoupling from the ch-projected slot (proof)}
In p15 D13 has an evanescent structure $E2_{(mn)\nu}=(\tilde g_{m\nu}p_n+\tilde g_{n\nu}p_m)p^2$ with
$A_{E2}(d)=3/(16(d-1))$ and UV pole $1/16$; p14r declares no evanescent counterterm. D13 enters the ch projection only
through the row $(S_0,\Gamma_1^{[2]})\,s_1\,h{:}h^2$:
\[
X_{D13}[c,h]=\int G_{(mn)\nu}(p)\,c^\nu(p)\,E^{(mn)(rs)}(p)\,h_{(rs)}(-p),
\]
where $E$ is the operator of the $h^2$ monomials of $S_\Psi^{(0)}$ (linearized Einstein--Hilbert). Its exact covariant
form is fitted from the frozen density and verified on all components; the fit is unique.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{L1.} $p_mE^{(mn)(rs)}=0$ as a covariant identity. Only $g_4\cdot p=p$ is used; no trace is taken, so the
identity holds exactly in $d$.
\item \textbf{L2.} $E2$ is longitudinal in $(mn)$.
\item \textbf{L3.} Therefore $E2\cdot E=0$ identically. The slot value is $0$ for every external assignment
(Q4S, QdS, mixed $\hat{}/\tilde{}$ components), exactly in $d$ and not merely $O(\epsilon)$.
\item \textbf{L4 (control).} The non-longitudinal $T1$ and $E1$ give nonzero slot values, so the map is not trivially
zero. $A_{T1}=A_{E1}=0$ for D13, so D13's whole ch-slot contribution is $0$.
\end{itemize}
Mutation controls: the gauge-fixed operator $q^2P$ in place of $E$, $E1$ in place of $E2$, and a wrong index slot
each make the $E2$ slot nonzero and are rejected. At one loop the ch projection is linear in $\Gamma_1$, so no product
of evanescent poles arises.

\emph{Outcome:} DECOUPLED (proof). No evanescent counterterm is added and no contract file changes for E2. The $E2$
pole remains a UV pole of the $\epsilon$-scalar component of the $K'\!\cdot c$ Green function (R6: retained and
recorded). Its renormalization matters only outside this projection, and it is not claimed here. D13 stays
\emph{regulated}, with a ch-slot contribution of $0$.

\subsection{Batch C: D01, D03 (covariant route)}
\textbf{Finding C1.} For rank-4 numerators, the p14r per-component R3 lift produces component sums quadratic in
$\tilde g$ (D03: 10 of 100 components). After the component sums, their abstract value cannot be recovered, because
the linear realization $\tilde g=(4-d)M$ is not faithful there. A finite component basis cannot carry a projector of
non-integer trace.

Batch C therefore uses a \emph{covariant route} that applies the same rules R1--R6 with free external indices only:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The exact covariant 4D numerator is fitted from the frozen export and verified as a polynomial identity on all
100 components. It is unique (upper external indices, off-diagonal weight 2).
\item The lift $\eta\to g_4$ is made.
\item Two independent loop routes are used: Feynman parameters with symmetric integration, and the frozen
\texttt{dred.reduce\_tensor} with the J library and S0. They agree exactly in $d$.
\item Then $\hat g=g_4-\tilde g$ on the free indices.
\end{enumerate}
D13 is reproduced exactly by this route (control), and the rules are unchanged (no contract change).

Further controls:
\begin{itemize}
\item The integrands are regenerated from $S_\Psi$ (D01 from the $\ell_3$ density, D03 from the ghost vertices) and
equal the export on 100 of 100 components.
\item The results are exchange symmetric.
\item The nonlocal $\log$ coefficient equals minus the pole.
\item The 4D poles lie in the span of the five p14r $h.h$ counterterm directions.
\end{itemize}
Seven mutations are each rejected: ghost-loop sign, symmetry factor, premature $d=4$, dropped $\tilde g$, external
index position, off-diagonal weight, and the component route with the linear realization.
